message.content: Now there is an issue: When pressing cancel, only the currenlty uploading file gets a "retry" button; all the other remaining files remain at "Not uploaded". I'm not sure how to fix this: You could change the "Cancel" button into a "Resume" button, but what about the cancelled file: Should it be reuploaded, or skipped?

content.text:
My take: turn the button into "Resume" once the batch is cancelled (i.e., whenever there are `idle` files and nothing is queued/uploading), and have it bulk re-enqueue just the `idle` files — leave the one that was mid-upload as `cancelled` with its own Retry button, same as error entries already work.

The tradeoff: this treats "cancel all" as two different severities — remaining files are merely paused (bulk-resumable), but the one you actually interrupted mid-flight requires a deliberate individual Retry. That's consistent with how `error` already behaves (no bulk-retry-all-errors button either), but it does mean clicking Resume won't restart 100% of what got cancelled — the user has to notice and click Retry on that one row too. The alternative (Resume also re-queues the cancelled file) is more "one click fixes everything" but blurs cancel and pause into the same action, which is arguably what confused users about the two buttons in the first place.
